newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panamanians protest against U.S. military presence.
newsitem.headline: Panamanians protest against U.S. military presence.

text.p: Hundreds of protesters staged a noisy demonstration against U.S. military presence in Panama on Thursday on the 33rd anniversary of bloody anti-U.S. riots.

Wearing T-shirts that said "no to bases," the protesters belonging to human rights groups, leftist student organisations and union groups unfurled banners and shouted "get out assassins" in front of the fenced-off headquarters of the U.S. Southern Command (Southcom) in Panama City.

The riots in 1964 started after Panamanian high school students entered what was then the U.S.-controlled Panama Canal Zone to hang a Panamanian flag. At least 22 Panamanians died in ensuing clashes involving U.S. soldiers and U.S. citizens living in the zone.

"Jan. 9 was a defining moment for proud Panamanians which showed the need to fight for the end of all foreign presence in Panama," human rights activist and Roman Catholic priest Conrado Sanjur said at Thursday's demonstration.
According to bilateral treaties, the United States will turn over control of the Panama Canal to Panama and withdraw all troops by Dec. 31, 1999.
